name: Netflix
tagline: World's largest subscription streamer, now adding ads, live events and games
facts: Ad tier 250M+ MAV; 2026 ad revenue target ~$3B
Co-CEOs Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters

strategy.label: Mission
strategy.text: Entertain the world: whatever your taste, wherever you live, give you stories and joy on demand.

strategy.label: Vision
strategy.text: Become the default home for TV time, the first app opened on every screen, globally.

strategy.label: Core strategy
strategy.text: Global originals plus local-language hits that travel; scale spreads content cost thinner than any rival can.

strategy.label: Moat
strategy.text: Recommendation data, brand, 190-country distribution, and a self-funding $18B+ content engine with no legacy TV to protect.

strategy.label: Key bet
strategy.text: Ads and live events (NFL Christmas, WWE Raw, boxing) to lift ARM; walked from WBD, took $2.8B fee.

strategy.label: Your view
strategy.text: Having stopped reporting subscribers, should Netflix chase reach in India with a cheaper ad tier or protect premium pricing?

customers.pain: Scattered content across many apps; too much time choosing what to watch
customers.why: Deep originals slate, best-in-class recommendations, reliable streaming quality worldwide

customers.pain: Premium price unaffordable; password sharing crackdown removed free access
customers.why: Mobile plan, ad tier, telco bundles (Jio, Airtel) lower entry price

customers.pain: Live sports locked in pay-TV bundles and many apps
customers.why: Marquee live events included in existing subscription, no extra fee

customers.who: Brands and agencies buying premium video
customers.pain: Linear TV reach declining; CTV inventory fragmented and poorly measured
customers.why: Engaged, hard-to-reach audiences, in-house ad tech suite, programmatic buying

customers.pain: Limited global distribution for local stories
customers.why: Upfront funding plus instant reach across 190 countries

products.name: Standard/Premium
products.desc: Ad-free tiers, 4K and extra screens on Premium

products.name: Mobile plan (India etc.)
products.desc: Single phone, SD, cheapest ad-free entry

products.name: Extra member
products.desc: Paid sharing add-on after password crackdown

portfolio.north_star: Monthly hours viewed per paying household
portfolio.key_metrics: Net adds, churn, ARM, engagement share of TV time
portfolio.guardrails: Churn after price hikes, content spend per hour viewed

products.name: Netflix Ads Suite
products.desc: In-house ad server, measurement and programmatic

products.name: Live events
products.desc: NFL Christmas games, WWE Raw, boxing, specials

products.name: Interactive ads
products.desc: New formats, pause and AI-generated creative

portfolio.north_star: Ad revenue per ad-tier monthly active viewer
portfolio.key_metrics: MAV, fill rate, CPMs, ad load, live concurrency
portfolio.guardrails: Ad-tier engagement and churn vs ad-free, stream failures

products.name: Netflix Games
products.desc: TV party games and mobile games, no ads

products.name: Netflix House
products.desc: Physical fan experiences in US malls

products.name: Licensing/merch
products.desc: Franchise merchandise from Stranger Things, Squid Game

portfolio.north_star: Members engaging with an IP beyond the show
portfolio.key_metrics: Game DAU, retention lift, merch revenue
portfolio.guardrails: Distraction from core video investment, brand fit

rows.how: Tiered monthly plans, regular price increases, paid sharing
CPM-based upfronts and programmatic via own ad stack
Drives acquisition, retention and high-CPM ad inventory

bullets.label: Revenue mix
bullets.text: ~94% subscription; ads ~6% of 2026 revenue (~$3B) but roughly doubling yearly.

bullets.label: Users vs payers
bullets.text: One payer per household, several viewers; ad tier 250M+ monthly active viewers in mid-2026.

bullets.label: Unit economics
bullets.text: Content is largely fixed cost; each new member is near-pure margin, lifting op. margin toward 31.5%.

bullets.label: Growth levers
bullets.text: Price hikes, ad monetisation, live events, paid sharing, emerging-market bundles.

bullets.label: Capital
bullets.text: ~$12.5B 2026 FCF; $25B buyback; $2.8B WBD break fee banked.

friction: Endless scrolling; choice paralysis at home screen
Repeated price hikes push serial churners to cancel
Password-sharing crackdown felt punitive to families
Shows cancelled after one season erode trust
Ad tier lacks some titles and downloads

competitors.label: Global SVOD
competitors.text: Prime Video, Disney+, Paramount+ with HBO Max, Apple TV

competitors.label: Free/attention
competitors.text: YouTube (top US TV share), TikTok, FAST channels

competitors.label: India
competitors.text: JioHotstar, Prime Video, ZEE5, SonyLIV, microdrama apps

competitors.label: Advertising
competitors.text: YouTube CTV, Amazon Prime Video ads, Roku, Hulu

competitors.label: Edge
competitors.text: Scale, global hit factory, recommendation engine, profitability rivals cannot match

competitors.label: Risk
competitors.text: YouTube winning TV time; ad ramp slower than promised; Paramount-WBD scale

news.label: Jul 2026
news.text: Q2 revenue $12.6B (+13%); ads $618M missed; $25B buyback authorised

news.label: May 2026
news.text: Upfront: ad tier reaches 250M+ global monthly active viewers

news.text: Q3 2026 results mid-Oct; can ads hit $3B and live sports scale?

sources: Netflix shareholder letters Q4 2025 and Q2 2026, Netflix India RoC filings FY25, S&P Global, press coverage. Metrics are PM estimates for interview prep. Prepared Oct 2026.
